B.N. Chowdhury with Parimal Chandra Guha—In support of the Ref.
Meah Abdul Gafur —For opposition.
parties:
Nesaruddin ------- Complainant
Vs.
Khalilur Rahman and others ------- Accused.
full_judgment: 9. In the present case when the application of Nesaruddin was at first filed on 30-2-76 Mr. A. R. Khan who was the Sub-Divisional Magistrate undoubtedly was not satisfied about apprehension of breach of the peace as stated by Nesaruddin in the application for which he referred the matter to R.C.O. Nazirpur for report. On 20-2-76 also the learned Magistrate was not satisfied about the apprehension of breach of the peace for which be did not pass any order receiving the second application of Nesaruddin and kept the matter pending awaiting receipt of report from the R.C.O. On 1-3-76 another Magistrate Mr. A. Islam who might be acting as Sub-Divisional Magistrate on that date only heard parties and passed the order for attachment of the land and appointment of the receiver. Save and except the application of Nesaruddin there was no other material before him for his satisfaction about apprehension of breach of the peace. It seems to me that he must not have applied his mind and did not pay attention to the order passed by Mr. A. R. Khan who was waiting for report from the R.C.O. From the report of the learned Magistrate it will appear that subsequent to passing of the impugned order the R.C.O. submitted his report dated 2-3-76. The learned Magistrate seeing the report of the R.C.O. and hearing the parties passed the order dated 10-3-76 in which it is stated that the first party Nesaruddin took possession on the basis of decree of the civil court which was subsequently set aside and hence the learned Magistrate was of the opinion that the disputed land was in the possession of the second party and to disturb their possession the case under section 145 Cr.P.C. was filed. It should be noted that the case was fixed on 30-3-76 awaiting report of the R.C.O. but on an off date i.e. 1-3-76 the learned Magistrate without Issuing any notice to the second party and without giving the second party any chance to be heard attached the disputed land and appointed a receiver under his order dated 1-3-76. The decision In the cases reported in 8 D.L.R 397, 13 D.L.R. (S.C.) 178 are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. In these cases any ground of satisfaction of the Magistrate was not stated But in the present case it was teen stated by the learned Magistrate that there was apprehension of breach of the peace. The decision reported in PLD 1933 Peshawar 88 is not also applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case for the reasons the impugned order seems to have been prejudicial to the seer ad party. The case reported in 21 DLR (W.P.) 119 undoubtedly supports the second party In which the view has been taken that omission to comply with a condition of jurisdiction in a criminal statute is not a mere irregularity but an illegality which renders subsequent orders illegal. In the facts and circumstances of the case It seems to me that the learned magistrate Mr. A Islam without applying his judicial mind and not paying attention to the order passed by Mr. A. R. Khan passed order for attachment of the land and appointment of the receiver on an of date. As such the impugned order dated 1-3-76 passel by the learned Magistrate Mr A. Islam is illegal and without jurisdiction.
